Venezuelan Telecommunications Workers Walk Out, Disrupting Industry Operations

CARACAS, June 12 — Thousands of workers in Venezuela’s telecommunications sector staged a walkout Wednesday, halting operations at switching centers and call centers across the country and causing widespread disruption to the industry’s core activities.

The strike, organized by the National Union of Telecommunications Employees (SINATEL), began at midnight after negotiations with employers over wage increases and benefits broke down. According to SINATEL, more than 7,000 technicians, engineers, and customer service agents from major operators including TelVen, RedCom, and CeluVoz joined the action, demanding a 40% salary hike to offset rising living costs.

“Our members are determined to continue the strike until our demands are met,” said union leader Laura Castillo in a statement. “Years of stagnant pay and deteriorating working conditions have left us with no choice.” Castillo added that minimal maintenance teams were in place to handle emergency situations, but most routine technical work and customer support had ceased.

Industry association spokesperson Jorge Ríos confirmed that several regional service centers and technical hubs had been forced to suspend regular operations, with field repairs and scheduled network upgrades postponed indefinitely. “We are urging all parties to return to the negotiating table as soon as possible to minimize further disruption,” Ríos said.

Analysts noted that the work stoppage has delayed the rollout of 4G and fiber-optic network expansion projects at multiple sites, with installation crews and project managers participating in the walkout. “The timing is critical, as the industry is already under pressure to modernize infrastructure,” said telecoms analyst María Zambrano.

Union officials reported that picket lines remained in place outside key company sites in Caracas, Maracaibo, and Valencia late Wednesday, with no immediate breakthrough in sight. Negotiations are expected to resume later this week.
